body: claimed: SKULL (Claude agent, mkinney fork, Linux box with sccache) · 2026-11-12 04:13 UTC · no branch (measurement) · plan: answer the five points on Linux (no-sccache run, cold vs warm cross-worktree build + hit rate + target size, both opt-outs, panic backtrace file:line, flecs C caching) in a comment; any breakage gets a PR or issue. Note: box has other builds running, timings are indicative.

## Linux measurement (SKULL worker, mkinney fork)

Measured on NeoTech/Camcraft `upstream/main` 3e9b8ae1 (PR #913 merged). Box: Linux, **8 cores**, 62 GB RAM, sccache 0.13.0, mold installed. **Other SKULL builds were running concurrently, so all timings are indicative only.** Load averages are the 1-min uptime figures from before and after each run. Each run used a fresh worktree with its own default `target/`. No `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` was exported. sccache ran on an isolated server (`SCCACHE_SERVER_PORT=4914`, own `SCCACHE_DIR`), so the shared default cache was untouched and the cold run started from an empty cache.

Test binary for points 2 and 5 is the same as #913: `cargo xtask gate test repair_fills_the_hole_and_undo_restores_the_facet_count --crate camcraft-app --binary repair_model --exact`.

| Run | Gate wall | target/ | sccache requests | Hits | Misses | Hit rate (Rust) | C/C++ hit/miss | Load avg (start to end) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A cold (empty cache, empty target) | 189 s | 1.4 G | 291 | 0 | 203 | 0% | 0 / 1 | 9.3 to 32.1 |
| B warm (same cache, other worktree, empty target) | 179 s | 1.4 G | 291 | 180 | 23 | 88.7% (88.6%) | 1 / 0 | 27.9 to 18.1 |

Non-cacheable calls: 80 (crate-type 62, incremental 8). The warm run saves compiler time per crate (the cold average compile was 2.9 s), but on this loaded box wall time barely moved, since the non-cacheable link and build-script work dominates.

**Comparison with #913 (Windows MSVC, also loaded):** cold 395 s baseline, sccache warm 177 s (about 2.2x), 77.8% cross-worktree hit rate. Here, 189 s cold vs 179 s warm (about 1.05x) at 88.7% hits. The hit rate reproduces. The wall-time gain did not, under this load. Re-measure on an idle box before judging the 3x goal. Done-means is not confirmed on Linux.

### Answers
1. **Without sccache (PATH with sccache removed):** `cargo xtask gate quick --dry-run` runs without error. `command -v sccache` was empty. `cargo xtask gate test v1_roundtrip_is_exact --crate camcraft-post --binary post_engine --exact` ran ok in 99 s. No "compile cache" line was printed, so no wrapper was set. Load 5.4 to 9.0.
2. **Cross-worktree cache:** see the table. Cold 189 s with 0% hits, warm 179 s with 88.7% hits, same cache, different worktree path, no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. Target 1.4 G each.
3. **Opt-outs (both win):**
   - Control (sccache on, no opt-out): 14 sccache compile requests, and the "compile cache: sccache on" line printed.
   - `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`: 0 sccache requests, no cache line. sccache was not contacted.
   - Pre-set `RUSTC_WRAPPER=<logging wrapper>`: the wrapper logged 4 rustc invocations, 0 sccache requests, no cache line. The pre-set wrapper wins.
4. **Panic backtrace:** a throwaway failing test in `crates/post/tests`, run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` on the lighter dev profile. The backtrace shows `crates/post/tests/zz914_panic.rs:4:49` for the panic site, plus `./tests/zz914_panic.rs:4:31` and `:2:16` for our frames, so file:line holds. Std frames show no line numbers, which is expected. Only the test frame was exercised, not a library frame. The change was discarded and the worktree is clean.
5. **flecs C code:** not cached on Linux. `flecs_ecs_sys` 0.2.1 `build.rs:236` compiles through `cc::Build`, which uses `CC`/`CXX` and does not go through `RUSTC_WRAPPER`. sccache did register one C/C++ request (miss cold, hit warm), but it is not from flecs and I did not identify it. Suggestion, not tested: `CC="sccache cc"` (and `CXX`) would route flecs through the cache. A PR is not needed for this measurement.

### Dry-run note
`cargo xtask gate quick --dry-run` in a detached worktree with no diff against main planned all four suites (sim, motion, app, ui), not a narrow set. That is probably expected for an empty diff, but a quick run on an empty diff does not look like "tests only what the diff touches". Not a breakage; noted for the maintainer.

### Breakage
None found. No issue filed, and no PR opened.

Environment cleanup: scratch worktrees removed and the port-4914 sccache server stopped (see final step).
Claim recorded for @mkinney - label and assignee set (only collaborators can set labels; your comment is the claim).
SKULL: claim released (stale-job sweep). The Linux measurement is posted above; left open for the maintainer to close.

Correction (SKULL) to point 5 of the Linux measurement above: flecs' C code **is** cached on Linux. cc-rs 1.8.0 (in Cargo.lock) prefixes `RUSTC_WRAPPER` to the C/C++ compiler when that wrapper is sccache (`rustc_wrapper_fallback`), and `cargo xtask gate` exports it since #913, so `flecs_ecs_sys`'s `cc::Build` goes through sccache. The single C/C++ request seen (miss cold, hit warm) was exactly that compile; a fresh worktree confirmed a cross-worktree C hit. The suggested `CC="sccache cc"` is not needed. Details: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/900#issuecomment-6832273019
